# Question

**Are city dwellers more likely than country dwellers to have mood and anxiety disorders?** Peen, Dekker, Schoevers & ten Have (2007) analysed the NEMESIS population survey across five urbanization levels; Lock⁵'s phase-2 question contrasts the most vs least urbanized.

## Data source

Published Table 2 counts from NEMESIS-1 (Peen et al. 2007) — near-exact reconstruction. Headline context: Peen, Schoevers, Beekman & Dekker (2010) meta-analysis.

# Exploratory analysis

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Mood and anxiety disorder rates by urbanization level (NEMESIS)"
u = df.assign(mood=df["mood_cases"] / df["n"],
              anx=df["anxiety_cases"] / df["n"])
x = np.arange(len(u))
w = 0.38
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.2))
ax.bar(x - w / 2, u["mood"], w, label="Mood disorders", color="#c76c6c")
ax.bar(x + w / 2, u["anx"], w, label="Anxiety disorders", color="#4c72b0")
ax.set_xticks(x, [s.replace(" ", "\n") for s in u["urbanization"]], fontsize=8)
ax.set_ylabel("Prevalence")
ax.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

# Methods & results

Two-proportion z (pooled) and Fisher exact for city vs country contrasts on each outcome, odds ratios with bootstrap CIs, and 100k-replicate randomization tests.

| Outcome | City vs country | OR | p |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mood disorders | 10.4% vs 5.3% (+5.1 pp) | 2.06 (bootstrap CI excludes 1) | z p = 3.7e-6 · Fisher p = 3.8e-6 · rand. p < 1e-5 |
| Anxiety disorders | 14.4% vs 10.8% (+3.6 pp) | 1.39 | z p = 0.0075 · rand. p = 0.008 |

# Decision

**Reject H₀ for both outcomes** — urbanicity is significantly associated with mood and anxiety disorders, matching the Peen et al. (2010) meta-analysis headline. Observational: urbanicity may proxy for other risk factors (social drift, crowding, pollution), so the causal pathway is open.
